subjects.name: US bombing of Cambodia and Laos

summary: German-born US National Security Advisor and Secretary of State Henry Kissinger helped prolong the Vietnam War, directed the secret bombing of Cambodia and Laos, and backed mass killings in Bangladesh and East Timor in the 1960s-70s.

evidence.note: Born 1923 in Furth, Germany, to a Jewish family
Family flees Nazi Germany for New York in 1938
Nuclear Weapons and Foreign Policy book and CFR report push limited nuclear war
1968: he leaks Paris peace-talk details to the Nixon campaign
Nixon names him National Security Advisor
Secret B-52 bombing of Cambodia planned and falsified via his office
Death tolls in Cambodia and Laos, unexploded ordnance still killing people
Operation Searchlight in East Pakistan while US backs Yahya Khan
FBI wiretap program on staff and journalists after the Cambodia leak
Ford and Kissinger visit Jakarta on eve of East Timor invasion
Pushes CIA covert funding of FNLA and UNITA in Angola
Legacy: centralized executive war powers still shaping US foreign policy

notes: Kissinger was alive at release (died 2023), so covered_span ends 2022. Setting capped at 6; Germany (childhood), Chile, Angola, Pakistan, India, China, Egypt/Israel, Rhodesia and Iraq also get segments. Roles: academic years at Harvard justify scientist-scholar; political-operative (1968 leak) was a close alternative.
